# Devaputta Saṁyutta (SN 2)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Devaputta Saṁyutta* (SN 2) is the second collection of the *Saṁyuttanikāya*, titled the "Linked Discourses on Godlings" [SuttaCentral]. It depicts the Buddha in dialogue with various deities or "godlings" (*devaputta*), a term treated as synonymous with the *devatā* of the preceding *Devatā Saṁyutta* (SN 1) [SuttaCentral]. While sharing a similar poetic dialogue structure with SN 1, this saṁyutta places a markedly greater thematic emphasis on renunciation and spiritual striving [SuttaCentral]. In his assessment of canonical chronology, Paul Kingsbury (drawing on G. C. Pande) observes that stanzas in the collection treating the goal of spiritual striving reflect characteristics of an early stratum of Buddhist poetry [Kingsbury 2002].
Several discourses from the *Devaputta Saṁyutta* occupy an enduring role in living Theravāda monastic and devotional practice [SuttaCentral]. In particular, the verses of Tāyana on energetic striving (SN 2.8) are frequently chanted by monastics, while the discourses concerning the moon and sun deities (SN 2.9 and SN 2.10) function as popular protective (*paritta*) chants [SuttaCentral].
The suttas in SN 2 preserve numerous cross-tradition parallels [SuttaCentral]. Curated parallels listed on SuttaCentral and automated cross-language alignments generated by DharmaNexus extensively correspond to both Chinese translations of the *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99 and the *Bieyi za ahan jing*, T 100) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Many verses also parallel the Sanskrit and Prakrit verse collections, including the *Udānavarga* (in Sanskrit and Central Asian Subaši recensions), the *Patna Dharmapada*, and the *Gāndhārī Dharmapada* [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. In addition, Sanskrit fragments (SF 276) and Tibetan translations correspond to the *Candrasūtra* (D 331) and *Sūryasūtra* (D 41) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Domestically within the Pali Tipiṭaka, DharmaNexus identifies thousands of matching segments, exhibiting its densest textual reuse with the *Devatā Saṁyutta* (SN 1), the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 4, AN 6), and the *Anāthapiṇḍikovāda Sutta* (MN 143) [DharmaNexus].
